newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen up after wages figures.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen up after wages figures.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen as opening higher on Tuesday after third-quarter figures for workers wages and benefits came in under expectations, analysts said.
Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management said: "It's lower than expected. Bonds should rally on this. We dodged one economic bullet."
"I think stocks will trade a little bit higher at the open but there will be trepidation going into the balance of the week with more economic indicators."
Orlando did not see much cause for concern with October consumer confidence due out at 1500 GMT. "That will be a good number."

Larry WachteL, market analyst at Prudential Securities, said: "The (ECI) index was weaker than expected and the bonds are rallying. But the market is obviously tired and needs consolidation. The entire framework of caution will not be superceded by one number."
